uncited: **Inputs:** A set of $n$ calibrated images of an object taken under different known light directions.
**Outputs:** Optimized 3D Gaussian parameters (position, covariance, color, opacity) representing the scene, from which surface normals and albedo maps are derived.
The scene is represented as a collection of 3D Gaussians.
**Initialization:** Initialize a set of 3D Gaussians to represent the scene.
**Rendering:** Render the normal map and albedo map.
**Gradient Descent:** Optimize Gaussian parameters (position, covariance matrix, color, opacity) using gradient descent.
*   Remove Gaussians that are too large or have too low opacity.
*   Clone or split Gaussians when more detail is needed.
*   **Cast Shadows:** The current model does not account for cast shadows (ombres portées), causing high angular estimation errors.
*   When interpretability of the reconstruction is prioritized over state-of-the-art accuracy on complex lighting conditions.
*   For calibrated photometric stereo with Lambertian surfaces.
*   When cast shadows are prominent and cannot be mitigated.
*   When higher accuracy is required than what GS-PS provides on non-trivial objects (e.g., Cat, Bear).
It builds on the Adaptive Spatio-Temporal 3D Gaussian Splatting method [9535-adaptive-spatio-temporal-3d-gaussian-splatting.md] by incorporating photometric and normal regularization losses.
